payload.title: TypeScript app extension compatibility for Rust server
payload.description:
Crate migration audit for Frick 0.4 found the blocker for non-trivial TS consumers: the Rust server has Rust-native traits for jobs, recurring target resolvers, projections, push/blob/search/policy/app-route seams, but Crate's production server is a TypeScript embedder with substantial app code.

Crate currently uses @fricken/server 0.3.1 with createFrickServer({ appRoutes, jobs.handlers, recurring.jobs, push.adapters, identityProviders }) plus post-boot projection registration. Those handlers cover Discogs/Square OAuth, webhooks, composed REST reads, durable marketplace jobs, recurring order polling, inventory/sales projections, outbound-sync projections, and silent push triggers. Rewriting all of that in Rust would be a full product/server port, not a package update.

Scope: provide a documented migration path for TypeScript app-owned server extensions on the Rust backend. Candidate designs: a sidecar/RPC protocol for app routes/jobs/projections/recurring target resolution/policy hooks; WASM plugin host; or an officially supported compatibility host that keeps TS handlers in-process/out-of-process while Rust owns the data plane. Include a Crate-sized fixture or conformance example so appRoutes + jobs + projections + recurring all run against frick-server 0.4 without rewriting product logic in Rust.

Relates to FR-296 (policy hooks) and FR-297 (custom app routes). This ticket is the broader adoption bridge for Frick-consuming apps that already invested in the TypeScript server extension surface.
